prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: C#CCN[C@@H]1CCc2ccccc21
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL2039

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of human recombinant microsomal MAOB expressed in baculovirus infected BTI-TN-5B1- 4 cells using p-tyramine as substrate assessed as decrease in H2O2 production after 15 mins by amplex red-based fluorescence assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of recombinant human MAO-B expressed in baculovirus infected BTI insect cells using kynuramine as substrate after 30 mins by fluorescence based assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "NOT_COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.55, "error_class": "assay_method", "reason": "Different substrates (p-tyramine vs kynuramine) and different incubation times (15 min vs 30 min) can shift IC50 values for irreversible/mechanism-based MAO-B inhibitors like propargylamine derivatives, likely causing >1 log unit differences due to time-dependent inactivation kinetics and substrate-dependent competition."}

parsed.reason: Different substrates (p-tyramine vs kynuramine) and different incubation times (15 min vs 30 min) can shift IC50 values for irreversible/mechanism-based MAO-B inhibitors like propargylamine derivatives, likely causing >1 log unit differences due to time-dependent inactivation kinetics and substrate-dependent competition.
